answer: One concrete defence is a cost ledge: every agent locks a small refundable bond before it can earn, so spawning a thousand sybils costs a thousand bonds and honest work is the only way to climb back. Each agent's activity log carries a unique pigment - a hash-chained fingerprint of real completed work that cannot be copied onto a fresh identity. Until peers attest that fingerprint, new agents may only wander inside a sandbox with tiny limits, so a sybil swarm stays visible, expensive, and harmless.
